title: Find out which Linux distribution and version I have
summary: Every Linux system stores the name and version of its distribution in the file /etc/os-release. Printing that file shows which Linux you run, such as Ubuntu or Fedora, and its version number.

aliases.text: which linux distro do i have
what version of linux am i running

steps.explain: Prints the release file that modern Linux systems have. Look for PRETTY_NAME (the full name with version) and VERSION_ID (the version number).
steps.gui: Open the system Settings app and look for an About page; on GNOME and KDE Plasma it shows the distribution name and version.
steps.expect: Lines such as PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS" and VERSION_ID="24.04", with your own system's name and version.

alternatives.explain: Shows only the name and version lines, without the rest of the file.
Print all available information about the Linux Standard Base and your distribution, including ID, description, release, and codename.

verify.expect: One line with your distribution name and version inside quotes.
